items.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995
items.q: his first band experience was with Andy Kirk

ctx.x: have become standards. Frank is now devoting his time to performing with small groups and composing new music. He was recently honored at a Town Hall Celebration in New York City.

Bill Hughes has been a familiar face in the Basie trombone section for many years. Born in Dallas, Texas, his first band experience was with Andy Kirk. He recorded with Frank Wess in 1952, then joined Basie for the first time in 1954, staying until ‘57. His recorded solo on “Magic” is a trademark and since 1964, Bill has been a presence with the Basie Orchestra, currently holding down the bass trombone chair.
Bill and Frank were interviewed together following a concert in Schenectady, New York on March 28, 1995, by Michael Woods and Monk Rowe.
